author: reek
body: A DTLS 1.3 handshake between two real endpoints, in one process, over datagrams, with no network.

author: reek
body: This is what the pure step-function discipline was for. The client and the server are the same code a device would run; the only thing missing is the socket, and the socket is the part that cannot be tested. We hand each datagram to the other side by hand, which also means we choose what arrives -- so loss and forgery are one line each.

author: reek
body: THE HANDSHAKE THIS COMPLETES IS NOT SECURE. There is no peer authentication in it: no Certificate, no CertificateVerify. What the two sides agree is an ANONYMOUS X25519 key, which resists a passive eavesdropper and does NOT resist an active man in the middle. This test going green means the transport works. It does not mean DTLS works, and it must not be quoted as if it did.

author: reek
body: The handshake Randoms. A device supplies real entropy here; a test supplies a fixed value so the exchange is reproducible. They are the caller's business, not the endpoint's -- and distinct from the private keys, which is the whole point of the field.

author: reek
body: Flight 2: the server will not allocate a thing. It answers with a HelloRetryRequest carrying a cookie derived from the client's address, and forgets the exchange ever happened.

author: reek
body: Flight 3: the client echoes the cookie.

author: reek
body: Flight 4: the cookie verifies, so NOW the server allocates: ServerHello plus its Finished.

author: reek
body: The client takes the ServerHello (completing the key exchange), then the server's Finished, and answers with its own.

author: reek
body: The server checks the client's Finished. Both sides are done.

author: reek
body: And they agreed on the same handshake secrets. This is the anonymous X25519 agreement, and it is the whole of what was proved.

author: reek
body: The cookie is bound to the client's address. A server that answers a ClientHello bearing someone else's cookie has learned nothing about who is really there -- so it must not proceed. Here the server is configured for a different address, so the cookie it recomputes will not match, and it must emit nothing.
